summary: Evaluate average double-shear stress in the upper boom-to-mast pivot pin and bearing stress in its central lug and outer clevis plates.
imageAttribution: Professor-supplied unannotated focused shop-crane photograph. It provides context only; no geometry, force, material property, allowable, or model identity is inferred from it.
idealizedImageAlt: Instructor reference showing the equivalent symmetric double-shear clevis connection at the upper boom-to-mast pivot.
problemStatement:
Analyze only the large upper boom-to-mast pivot pin, where the adjustable boom rotates relative to the mast assembly. Do not analyze the smaller lower hydraulic-ram pin or another fastener.

Replace the selected connection with an instructor-assigned symmetric double-shear clevis: one central boom lug carries the full equivalent transverse force F, two outer mast-clevis plates carry F/2 each, and the pin has two shear planes. The force, geometry, and allowables are teaching inputs, not measurements or manufacturer data.
engineeringGoal: Calculate average pin double-shear stress and central/outer plate bearing stresses, compare each with its assigned allowable, identify the dynamically governing included mode, evaluate load, diameter, and thickness sensitivities, and state a limited connection assessment without claiming crane certification.
